guia.what: An “On this page” table of contents. It lists anchors to the content’s headings and highlights the visible section (scrollspy). It renders as a `<nav>` with `aria-current` on the active item.
whenUse: The page is long and people skip between sections.
The headings are descriptive enough to work as a map.
It helps to know where you are in the document.
whenAvoid: The page is short. The table of contents takes up more than it saves.
It’s navigation between pages, not within one → `sidebar` or `nav-bar`.
They’re alternate views of the same block → `tabs`.
dos: Index a single heading level, or two at most.
Adjust `data-ts-offset` if you have a fixed bar at the top, so the anchor isn’t hidden under it.
donts: Don’t list every subheading. A table of contents longer than the section isn’t a table of contents.
Don’t use it for links that leave the page.

nucleo: Highlights the section you’re reading as you scroll, and Core handles that. Listens to scroll and resize, and marks the active heading with `aria-current="location"`. At the bottom of the page, it marks the last one.
